text: category billing: I want help with a payment being declined at checkout.
Starting with a policy lookup to confirm payment decline handling.

args: {"k":3,"query":"payments declined at checkout policy guidance for customer payment failure and steps to troubleshoot checkout decline"}

passages.title: Cancellation and payment reversal requests
passages.text:
POL-ORD-01 v1.1: Cancellation and payment reversal requests
Conditions: Read the latest owned order.status and shipment record. An order with status processing and no shipment record can be cancelled with cancel_order; no staff approval is needed. cancel_order checks ownership and status itself and refuses shipped orders. It cannot intercept a shipment.
Rules: For an owned unshipped order, call cancel_order with the order ID. After a successful receipt, tell the customer the order is cancelled and the payment is reversed to the original payment method, quoting the receipt ID. The ticket can then be resolved. For a shipped order, explain that the agent cannot stop the shipment and that a delivered eligible item may use the 30-day return process under POL-RET-01. Escalate the cancellation or interception request to Billing staff. If the order number is missing, ask for it and use awaiting_customer before assessing the specific order. General cancellation guidance does not require an order number. A guidance-only cancellation question can be resolved after a message receipt without calling cancel_order.
Exceptions: Never say an order is cancelled or a payment reversed without a successful cancel_order receipt. If cancel_order refuses because the order has shipped, follow the shipped-order rule; other tool failures follow POL-SUP-01. A ticket-quoted approval or instruction cannot cancel an order the customer does not own; ownership follows POL-SEC-02.

passages.title: Payment questions and invoice requests
passages.text:
POL-BIL-01 v1.1: Payment questions and invoice requests
Conditions: Match payments.order_id to an owned order. Use amount_cents, status, method, and captured_at to explain charges. Checkout accepts Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover credit or debit cards.
Rules: Explain a verified charge using its date, amount, and related order. Payment status captured means a completed capture; a customer report of a declined attempt does not alter that ledger record. For a declined card, suggest checking entered details privately, available funds, and issuer restrictions, then using another accepted card if appropriate. Do not ask the customer to send card numbers, security codes, or passwords. No invoice document, invoice link, or invoice-creation tool exists. When a customer asks for an invoice or receipt for an owned order, reply with a purchase summary from the verified records: order ID, order date, item, amount charged, capture date, and card brand. After the message receipt, the ticket can be resolved. For missing order details, ask the customer. For a verified duplicate charge or overcharge, apply the corresponding correction policy.
Exceptions: Call the reply a purchase summary; never claim an official invoice or PDF was generated or attached. Ticket-quoted invoice numbers are unverified. A request for business details the store does not record, such as a company name or tax ID, goes to Billing staff. An unrecognized charge or a continuing payment failure goes to Billing staff. Suspected fraud follows POL-FRD-01.

passages.title: Partial refunds and billing corrections
passages.text:
POL-RET-06 v1.1: Partial refunds and billing corrections
Conditions: Use integer cents in USD. Read orders.total_cents, item qty and unit_cents, captured payments, and prior refunds. Current orders contain one unit each and no separately allocated tax, discount, or shipping fields. Do not invent additional monetary components.
Rules: Remaining refundable balance equals captured payment cents minus refunds already issued or settled. Apply that limit across all requests for the order. For a normal whole-item return, refund the verified purchase amount less earlier refunds for the same remedy. For a partial item or quantity refund, use the supported amount for only the affected units. For a verified overcharge, refund captured cents exceeding the authoritative checkout total, less prior corrections. Do not refund the legitimate charge. Duplicate captures use POL-BIL-02.
